newsitem.title: USA: HP cleared to market InkJet cartridges.
newsitem.headline: HP cleared to market InkJet cartridges.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co said Monday a ruling by a federal judge allows it to continue marketing a new design of popular InkJet printer cartridges geared to be more reliable than earlier versions.

A spokesman for Hewlett-Packard said the federal judge's ruling, handed down late Friday, found that the company's packaging used on some of the old-style cartridges shipped recently incorrectly picture the new cartridges.
Hewlett-Packard is awaiting a hearing set for July 23 to receive specific terms of an injunction in the case, but it does not expect these to be financially material, he said.

Jeremy James, a spokesman for HP's consumer products group based in San Diego, Calif., said the judge had ruled against most of Nu-Kote's motion, while finding use of depictions of the new cartridges in packaging containing older-style cartridges constituted false labelling.
"The Judge said we can continue to manufacture the (new) bottom ink filled cartridges, which is the far more substantive issue," James said.
"We need to await the judge's specific terms on the packaging injunction," he added.
"However, our belief at this time is should the judge require us to produce new packaging for the top filled cartridges, the cost will not have a material impact on HP's finances," he said.
James said HP managers had estimated the cost that could be incurred in rectifying the packaging of older style cartridges would be in the $3 million to $6 million range.

Nu-Kote said in a statement issued Sunday that Federal Judge James Ware in San Jose, Calif., had ruled the packaging to be "literally false" in incorrectly depicting the cartridges it contains and had set a hearing for July 23 to specify exact terms of an injunction in the case.

Nu-Kote's motion for an injunction is part of ongoing litigation between the two companies. Hewlett-Packard originally sued Nu-Kote for patent infringement and Nu-Kote filed a counterclaim on anti-trust grounds.

Hewlett-Packard said it had redesigned the cartridges, including its popular HP51626A and HP51629A used in some DeskJet printers and OfficeJet multifunction and fax machines, to improve reliability by moving the fill hole to the bottom.

Nu-Kote said it expected a jury trial over damages on the packaging issue. HP said the packaging was intended to simplify the buying process and it believes it will prevail in any subsequent litigation over the package design.
